summary.bluf: Intruders exploited CVE-2026-41234 in Harbor Ledger's FerryGate server on 14 October 2026 and copied customer contact details. Defenders running FerryGate 9.0 to 9.4.1 should patch to 9.4.2 and hunt for web shells.
summary.leadership: A payments firm lost customer names and email addresses through a flaw in a file transfer product. Firms using the same product should update it this week.
summary.exposure: [ANALYST CONFIRMS] Do we run FerryGate 9.0 to 9.4.1 anywhere, and is it internet-facing?
summary.takeaway: Patch FerryGate to 9.4.2 and check web roots for unknown .aspx files.
summary.org_context: Financial services, Europe, FerryGate in the DMZ
summary.relevance: We run FerryGate in the DMZ, so the initial access path in C01 applies to us. The data taken (C04) matches what our own transfer servers hold.
summary.scope: The October 2026 intrusion at Harbor Ledger through FerryGate. Out of scope: the unrelated 2025 phishing incident at the same firm.
summary.attribution_statement: Northlight Research names Crimson Ferry, and the actor listed the victim on its leak site; police have arrested one suspect. The victim has not named an actor.
summary.glance_victim: Harbor Ledger, a European payments firm
summary.glance_type: Intrusion through a vulnerable file transfer server
summary.glance_impact: Customer names and email addresses copied
summary.glance_attribution: Crimson Ferry named by one researcher; not confirmed
summary.validation: check passed; the audit found no High items. One summarised source could not be quote-checked.

sources.title: Breach at Harbor Ledger: what we know

ledger.claim: The intruders exploited CVE-2026-41234 in Harbor Ledger's FerryGate server on 14 October 2026.
ledger.quote: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in our FerryGate file transfer server on 14 October.

ledger.claim: Harbor Ledger detected unusual activity on the FerryGate server at 14:05 UTC on 21 October 2026.
ledger.quote: On 21 October 2026 at 14:05 UTC we detected unusual activity on our FerryGate file transfer server.

ledger.claim: Harbor Ledger isolated the affected server on 22 October 2026.
ledger.quote: We isolated the affected server on 22 October and engaged an outside forensic firm.

ledger.claim: The intruders copied customer names and email addresses from the server.
ledger.quote: Some customer names and email addresses were copied from the server.

ledger.claim: Harbor Ledger says no payment card data was affected.
ledger.quote: No payment card data was affected.
ledger.corroboration: single originator: Harbor Ledger (S01), a statement that favours the victim

ledger.claim: CVE-2026-41234 lets an unauthenticated attacker run code on FerryGate 9.0 to 9.4.1, and 9.4.2 fixes it.
ledger.quote: CVE-2026-41234 is an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in FerryGate versions 9.0 to 9.4.1.

ledger.claim: The intruders dropped a web shell named health.aspx, and w3wp.exe spawned cmd.exe on the appliance.
ledger.quote: We observed the intruders drop a web shell named health.aspx after exploiting CVE-2026-41234.

ledger.claim: Crimson Ferry listed Harbor Ledger on its leak site on 22 October 2026.
ledger.quote: Crimson Ferry listed Harbor Ledger on its leak site on 22 October 2026.

ledger.claim: The appliance first contacted the attacker's server on 12 October 2026.
ledger.quote: Harbor Ledger's appliance first contacted the attacker's server on 12 October 2026.

ledger.claim: Metro Police arrested a man on 29 October on suspicion of taking part in the intrusion; he is an alleged participant and has not been convicted.
ledger.quote: Metro Police arrested a 31-year-old man on 29 October on suspicion of taking part in the intrusion.

ledger.claim: Harbor Ledger disclosed the incident publicly on 23 October 2026.
A news digest says the attackers stole customer contact details.
ledger.quote: The attackers stole the contact details of every customer.
ledger.corroboration: single originator: Harbor Ledger, relayed by S08

ledger.claim: No source reports any encryption or destructive payload.
Crimson Ferry is roughly even chance to be responsible for the breach (low confidence), resting on one researcher's attribution and the actor's own leak-site listing.
Further FerryGate victims are likely to emerge in the coming weeks (moderate confidence), because the flaw needs no credentials and many hosts remain unpatched.
